section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains why the name Tzevaot is not mentioned in the Torah but only in the Prophets, relating it to the level of Atzilus embodied by Moshe Rabbeinu versus the lower worlds.
section.t: And this is why the name Tzevaot is not mentioned in the Torah, only in the Prophets specifically,
for Moshe Rabbeinu was the soul and conduct of Atzilus,
therefore he was called Moshe, from “for from the water I drew him,”
water, wisdom, is the aspect of Atzilus.
And likewise the Torah, which was given through Moshe and is called by his name, as it is written,
“Remember the Torah of Moshe My servant,” is the aspect of Atzilus.
Therefore the name Tzevaot is not mentioned in the Torah,
for the name Tzevaot indicates
(as above)
Ein Sof as it is drawn down into created beings,
which are below Atzilus.
And this is
in the manner of what is said
regarding Yehoshua: “And he said, ‘No, for I am the captain of the host of Hashem; now I have come.’”
And our sages, of blessed memory, said,
“Now I have come, but your teacher Moshe did not receive [this].”
For in the days of Moshe,
“the face of Moshe was like the face of the sun,”
there was the drawing down of the aspect of Atzilus,
and also the conduct of wars
was not through the captain of the host of Hashem, but as it is written,
“Hashem will fight for you.”
For this is what happened at the Exodus from Egypt and the Splitting of the Sea: there were revealed miracles that departed entirely from the ways of nature, with no garment of nature at all,
because the war was through the Name Havayah,
the aspect of Atzilus.
But after the passing of “the face of Moshe like the face of the sun,” and the conduct was through “the face of Yehoshua like the face of the moon,”
then specifically the captain of the host of Hashem came,
“now”
(specifically)
“I have come.”
And although even then,
(through the conduct of war being through the captain of the host of Hashem)
there were several miracles above nature,
nevertheless, the war as a whole was somewhat within garments of nature,
and not like the war in the days of Moshe, which was entirely above garments of nature,
“Hashem will fight for you.”
And this is the matter of the name Tzevaot, which was drawn down through the prophets,
“A sign is He in His host,”
that even in the created beings of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah
(host)
there will be a sign of He Himself, literally, in His host,
that even in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, He and His organs shall be one, as in Atzilus.
And this matter is above the aspect of the captain of the host of Hashem
(which was with Yehoshua),
for the captain of the host of Hashem is an angel,
but the name Tzevaot is among the seven names that may not be erased,
for even in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, He and His organs become one.
And this is why the name Tzevaot was innovated through the prophets,
for the prophets drew down that even in the vessels of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah there should be the enclothing of Ein Sof, blessed be He, in ultimate unity,
as in the vessels of Atzilus,
and through this He is called by the name Tzevaot,
just as He is called by the names
(E-l,
Elokim, etc.)
which indicate the vessels of Atzilus
(because He and His organs are one),
for even the hosts
(the term for armies,
the legions of souls and angels of Beriah)
become one with Him, blessed be He,
as explained at length in Torah Ohr.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the innovation of the name Tzevaot as taught by the Alter Rebbe, whereby even in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, He and His organs become one through the service of Israel.
section.t: And now, regarding the above matter of the name Tzevaot, that He and His organs are one even in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,
the Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, writes
that in the Pri Etz Chaim this is not found.
From this it is implied that this is an innovation of the Alter Rebbe,
as is evident from the fact that the Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, does not cite any other source for this.

And the magnitude of the innovation and elevation of the name Tzevaot, which is accomplished through the service of the children of Israel when they are in the state and condition of the time of the prophets, is understood
(after the time of “the face of Moshe like the face of the sun”),
and particularly when Israel is in the state and condition of the time of the later prophets, which was at the end of the First Temple and the beginning of the time of exile,
and likewise in the time thereafter,
that even in the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, which in themselves are created and separate beings
[for the matter of “He and His organs are one” is in Atzilus,
the world of unity]
there shall be “He and His organs are one” as in Atzilus.
And it can be said that this is the explanation of the statement that Tzevaot is a holy name, and yet it is called after His host
(as in the Gemara),
after Israel,
for this—that Tzevaot is a holy name,
meaning that even in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, He and His organs are one—
is accomplished through the service of Israel,
as above.
And this is accomplished through drawing down light from a most supernal place,
which is higher even than the aspect of the Torah
(as it was revealed in the time of Moshe).
For in the Torah the name Tzevaot is not mentioned
(meaning that from the perspective of the aspect of the Torah,
the matter of “He and His organs are one” is only in Atzilus),
and in order for there to be “He and His organs are one” even in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, one must draw down from a higher place.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the drawing down of this light is achieved through the service of refining the sparks, as taught by the Baal Shem Tov and elaborated by the Rebbe Maharash.
section.t: And now, this drawing down is through the service of refining the sparks.
For behold, the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov is known,
that in every object found in the possession of a Jew there are holy sparks that belong to the root of his soul.
And with this he explains why the Torah is sparing with the money of Israel
(even though it is only their money),
for since the money
(and likewise other things)
belongs to a Jew,
this indicates
(for all matters are with Divine Providence)
that these sparks belong to the root of his soul,
and the refinement of these sparks is part of his service,
and by refining the sparks, purifying them, and elevating them to their root, they also add elevation to him.
For similarly it was in the Egyptian exile,
that through “they emptied out Egypt,” making it like a marsh without fish and like a net without grain,
they refined the sparks belonging to the hidden world
(like a marsh without fish)
and the sparks belonging to the revealed world
(like a net without grain),
and through this an elevation was also effected in Israel.
And as the Rebbe Maharash explains
at length regarding the matter of “And it came to pass when Pharaoh sent out the people,” that he sent out branches and twigs and made fruit above, “the people,”
that through the sparks they refined in the Egyptian exile, an addition and increase was effected in them.
For this is what is said
(regarding the Egyptian exile)
“And I will sow her for Me in the land,”
the matter of sowing is as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
“Does a person sow a kor
except in order to bring forth several korin?”
That is,
that Israel being sown in the Egyptian exile was for the sake of the addition effected in them through the refinement of the sparks.
As the Rebbe Maharash explains at length, several details regarding the addition effected through the refinement of the sparks.
